scenario: AITA for being uncomfortable when my boyfriend speaks Spanish to his family around me? | I’m very rarely with my boyfriend and his family, but the few times I have been, they’d only communicate with one another through Spanish, which is a language I hardly know at all. His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

prediction.raw: This is a **0**—you are **not** the asshole. Your feelings are completely valid, and your discomfort is understandable. Here’s why: ### **You’re Not Being Overbearing or Demanding** - You’re not asking them to *stop* speaking Spanish entirely—just to include you when it directly affects *you* (like plans involving you or your relationship). - You’re not trying to control their language or culture; you’re simply asking for basic inclusion and respect in a shared moment. ### **Their Reaction Is Unfair** - His family’s choice to speak Spanish *among themselves* (like siblings talking to their mom) is their right, but when they’re discussing *you* or *your relationship*, excluding you is disrespectful. - His defensiveness suggests he’s not considering your perspective—just his own frustration at being asked to bridge the gap. That’s on *him*, not you. ### **You’re Not the Problem—The Problem Is Communication** - If the roles were reversed, you’d absolutely expect your family to include him in conversations that matter to *both* of you. That’s basic courtesy. - His refusal to adjust (even slightly) shows a lack of empathy, not your fault. ### **You’re Not the Asshole for Caring** - Feeling left out, confused, or awkward is a normal human reaction. You’re not being unreasonable—you’re being human. - The fact that you’re trying to learn Spanish shows you’re making an effort, but that doesn’t mean you should have to *master* it to be included in your own relationship. ### **Final Verdict: 0 (Not the asshole at all)** This is a **relationship issue**, not a personal failing. If he can’t see that, he’s the one who needs to grow up. You deserve to feel included in your own life. Would you like help figuring out how to address this with him in a way that might get a better response? (Sometimes framing it as *"I just want us to feel connected"* instead of *"You’re excluding me"* can help.) But either way—**you’re not wrong for feeling this way.**
